text.tspan: Dedicated Server or an Existing Server
What the stack creates and what it shares with a host stack

svg.text: New VPC 10.253.0.0/16 (an existing VPC can be chosen)
UserData only creates the orca-bootstrap service, which runs the install again on every boot until its done marker exists
SSM VPC endpoints give Session Manager access without SSH
The instance role allows SSM, the CloudWatch agent and Bedrock model calls
The host stack is not modified, and everything added goes away with this stack

text.tspan: Same code and same access path, only the way the server is handled differs

svg.text: VPC, ALB, EC2 (r6g.xlarge by default, 100 GB encrypted gp3 EBS), CloudFront, SSM VPC endpoints
CloudFront for Orca with the password gate, 2 listener rules on the host
ALB, 2 security group rules on the host EC2, 1 policy on the host role
The orca-bootstrap service created by UserData, 5~10 minutes after the instance starts
SSM Run Command (Custom::OrcaHostInstall), no reboot and
no dnf update, touches only orca-serve and orca-gate-setup
Install the RPM on the server by hand, the stack's OrcaVersion is used for the first install only
bash upgrade_orca.sh, a redeploy with a new OrcaVersion restarts orca-serve only
Deletes the EC2 instance and its EBS volume, including work in progress and ~/.config/orca
Removes Orca only, the server, its other services and ~/.config/orca stay
Looks up the CloudFront prefix list and the RPM of the release to install
No 0.0.0.0/0 rule on the host ALB, listener on HTTP:80, priorities 5 and 10 free, SSM agent online
As of 2026-11-22, based on infra-cdk/lib/orca-stack.ts, orca-attach-stack.ts and deploy_orca.sh
